description: Six-panel TEM figure (3 rows × 2 columns) of micrographs, stated in the caption to be bright-field images captured at two different locations in each alloy: (a,b) 28Mn0Ni, (c,d) 28Mn5Ni and (e,f) 15Mn5Ni, all in the HR + CR + 1173 K condition. Every panel has a 2 µm scale bar at lower left, a white panel letter in the corner, and the alloy name printed vertically along the left of each row. (a) shows a large austenite grain labelled "γ" with straight, angular planar bands meeting in triple-junction-like geometry and no resolvable second-phase particles; (b) shows the same kind of faceted, angular banded contrast with γ labelled, the dark bands dominant. (c) shows a strongly heterogeneous deformed matrix (dark strained regions next to bright recrystallized grains) with white solid arrows and yellow broken arrows both labelled "B2" marking bright particles of a coarser and a finer class. (d) shows bright equiaxed grains with the same two B2 particle classes. (e) and (f) show a darker, heavily strained matrix with bright B2 particles (white arrows) and finer B2 (yellow broken arrows). The set demonstrates that at 1173 K the Ni-free alloy is precipitate-free whereas the Ni-containing alloys still contain intragranular B2.
measured_quantities: B2 particle size (nm) - cited for companion 973 K figure, not printed here

observations.observation: The figure is a 3×2 grid of TEM micrographs; rows are labelled vertically, from top to bottom, 28Mn0Ni, 28Mn5Ni and 15Mn5Ni, and each panel carries a 2 µm scale bar and a white letter (a)-(f).
In panels (a) and (b) only the austenite grain is labelled ('γ'); no arrow-marked precipitate particles and no second-phase contrast that can be resolved as discrete particles are visible.

In panels (c)-(f) two arrow styles are used to mark particles, both labelled 'B2': solid white arrows on the larger bright particles and broken yellow arrows on the finer bright particles; some marked particles sit on grain boundaries and some inside grains.

Panel (c) shows the most heterogeneous structure, with dark, heavily strained regions bordering bright recrystallized grains, whereas panel (d) of the same alloy is dominated by brighter equiaxed grains.
The caption states the six panels are bright-field images captured at two different locations for each of the 28Mn0Ni (a,b), 28Mn5Ni (c,d) and 15Mn5Ni (e,f) alloys in the HR + CR + 1173 K condition.
The caption labels the panels 'bright-field', yet panel (b) shows strong faceted dark/bright diffraction-type contrast; the image alone cannot confirm bright-field acquisition for (b).
The citing text states that no secondary phase precipitates were seen in the 28Mn0Ni alloy after heat treatment at 1173 K (Fig. 7a and b).

The citing text states that in the Ni-containing steels heat treated at 1173 K the fraction of intragranular B2 precipitation decreased with increasing recrystallized austenite fraction, indicating that highly strained regions are preferential nucleation sites for these precipitates.
The citing text states that the composition profile of B2 was obtained by TEM-EDS and is reported in Table 2.

The citing text states that low-temperature (973 K) heat-treated samples contained a higher volume fraction of deformed austenite together with κ-carbides than the samples heat treated at 1173 K, comparing Figs. 6 and 7.

The citing text states that the dark-field images of the companion figure (Fig. 6) were captured from (010) satellite spots corresponding to κ-carbide in SAED patterns; no κ-carbide label or SAED inset appears in this figure.

The citing text attributes the reduced ductility of low-temperature heat-treated Ni-containing LDS alloys to lower strain-hardening ability and to crack initiation controlled by second-phase particles.

subfigures.description: TEM micrograph of 28Mn0Ni (HR + CR + 1173 K), 2 µm scale bar; a large austenite grain labelled 'γ' with straight angular planar bands/traces meeting at a triple junction; no arrow-marked precipitates and no resolvable second-phase particles.

TEM micrograph of 28Mn0Ni, 2 µm scale bar; strongly faceted, angular banded contrast with dark bands in a lighter matrix, one region labelled 'γ'; again no arrow-marked precipitate particles. The faceted dark/bright geometry resembles dark-field-like diffraction contrast although the caption states bright-field.

TEM micrograph of 28Mn5Ni, 2 µm scale bar; highly heterogeneous microstructure with dark, heavily strained/deformed regions adjacent to bright recrystallized grains. White solid arrows and yellow broken arrows, both labelled 'B2', point to bright particles of a coarser and a finer size class, some at grain boundaries and some intragranular.

TEM micrograph of 28Mn5Ni, 2 µm scale bar; brighter, mostly equiaxed recrystallized grains. White solid arrows labelled 'B2' mark larger bright particles and yellow broken arrows labelled 'B2' mark fine bright particles inside the grains.
TEM micrograph of 15Mn5Ni, 2 µm scale bar; dark, high-contrast strained matrix with several bright, rounded/angular particles annotated 'B2' by white solid arrows.

TEM micrograph of 15Mn5Ni, 2 µm scale bar; dark speckled heavily deformed region with fine bright particles marked by yellow broken arrows labelled 'B2'. Individual particle detail is at the limit of the supplied resolution.

unreadable_items: No numeric axis or particle-size values are printed on any panel; all sizes (κ-carbide 10-60 nm, intragranular B2 5-20 nm, intergranular B2 50-200 nm) come from the citing text, not from pixels.
Panel (f): individual fine B2 particles are only marginally resolvable at the supplied resolution.

The arrow convention (solid white = coarser/intergranular B2 vs broken yellow = fine/intragranular B2) is not defined in this figure's caption; it was inferred from the citing description of the companion figure.
